topic: The p-n Junction and Depletion Layer
title: The Wall That Builds Itself Explained Simply | PUC, CBSE and ISC
description:
Aarav opens a dead phone charger and finds tiny black parts with a stripe at one end. Inside each is just p-type silicon joined to n-type silicon, yet together they act like a one-way gate. Where does the gate come from? It builds itself at the joint. We start with two rooms and an open door (diffusion), then watch the real crystal: electrons diffuse from n to p, holes from p to n, they meet and fill each other, and the fixed donor and acceptor ions they leave behind form the depletion layer.

Those ions make an electric field from n to p that drives a drift current against diffusion, until the two are equal and no net current flows. On a live breadboard the oscilloscope shows the diffusion and drift currents settling to equilibrium while the readout tracks the layer width and the barrier potential (about 0.7 V in silicon), drawn as an energy hill an electron must climb. Worked example: the field in a 0.5 micrometre layer and the least energy to cross. Then the exam trap (a voltmeter cannot read the barrier), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a fact card to screenshot.

This is Episode 40 of PUC Electronics. Karnataka I PUC Electronics Ch 6: Semiconductors, Diodes and Applications of Diodes | NCERT/CBSE Class 12 Physics Ch 14: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits | ISC Class 12 Physics: Electronic Devices (p-n junction).
